# Lab 9.12: Apply Predefined Org Policies

## What We Are Going to Do
Enforce three common predefined constraints on a project and test each one.

## Steps

1. **Block external IP addresses on VMs.** Create `no-ext-ip.yaml`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • YAML
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">name: projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/policies/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
spec:
  rules:
  - denyAll: true</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud org-policies set-policy no-ext-ip.yaml</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Enforce public access prevention on buckets.** Create `no-public-buckets.yaml`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • YAML
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">name: projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/policies/storage.publicAccessPrevention
spec:
  rules:
  - enforce: true</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud org-policies set-policy no-public-buckets.yaml</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Allow only your own domain in IAM.** In the console, go to **Organization policies**, search **Domain restricted sharing**, choose **Override parent's policy**, add a rule **Allow** with your Cloud Identity customer ID (from `gcloud organizations list`), and save.

4. **Test all three.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances create orgpol-vm --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-micro
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=user:someone@gmail.com --role=roles/viewer</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Both fail with an org policy error. Making a bucket public also fails.

5. **See the effective policy.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud org-policies describe compute.vmExternalIpAccess --project=$PROJECT_ID --effective</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud org-policies delete compute.vmExternalIpAccess --project=$PROJECT_ID
gcloud org-policies delete storage.publicAccessPrevention --project=$PROJECT_ID
gcloud org-policies delete iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains --project=$PROJECT_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| VM with external IP | Blocked |
| Public bucket | Blocked |
| Outside Gmail user | Cannot be granted a role |
| Existing resources | Not changed by new policies |
